target_customer: Brazilian formal-sector employees, reached through employers or directly, who need short-term credit before payday
problem: Many Brazilian workers rely on expensive overdrafts and payday-style credit. Facio offers salary advances and payroll-linked credit at lower, transparent cost.
business_model: Consumer lending and salary advance with fees and interest, funded partly through a planned receivables fund; operates as a correspondent for a licensed credit institution
product_category: Fintech: earned wage access and personal credit (Brazil)

founders.name: Saulo Tristao
founders.background_notes: A press item calls him a former SumUp executive and former Olympic athlete.

founders.name: Marcio Dos Santos
founders.background_notes: 15 plus years in software, machine learning infrastructure, per YC page.

founders.name: Ticiano Vieira
founders.background_notes: Helped build SumUp per YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Credit scoring from bank data, payroll integrations and a regulated lending structure are standard fintech engineering with hard parts around risk and compliance.

defensibility.rationale: Employer agreements and repayment data help, and licensing partners are needed, but many lenders offer similar credit.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No evidence of acquisition or copying found. A 2026 article describes Facio as one of several apps in the category.

market_need_then: A Brazil Journal piece quotes the company calling the bank overdraft a jurassic product, indicating high-cost credit pain. No dated market sizing was read.

branding.domain_note: Uses facio.com.br, a Brazilian country domain, not facio.com.

identity.voice_and_tone: Simple and fast: Credito Facil, Dinheiro em 2 minutos

branding.brand_signature: Ta Facio promotion with scratch-card prizes and a R$10,000 raffle (company site)
branding.community_and_virality: The company site claims over 6 million customers; no independent community evidence.

brand_strength.rationale: Claimed 6M plus customers and consumer app marketing suggest recognition in Brazil, but the claim is the company's own and no brand press was found.

pivots.to: Adds payroll-deducted loans, savings and direct consumer credit
pivots.why: Brazil Journal reports the company also launched consignado and savings; later site shows direct personal credit. Exact dates not found.

outcome_analysis: Facio raised a $5M seed in 2020 led by Monashees and has stayed active with a team of about 36 on YC and a site claiming more than 6 million customers. It moved from employer-based salary advances toward broader credit, which fits large market demand in Brazil. Later round details are unverified, so the strength of traction is only partly supported.
notes: Seed cross-checked between Brazil Journal and Crunchbase News (both USD 5M). A startups newsletter cited R$25M with R$6M raised earlier, so the real number may differ. CB Insights and VCBacked list a Series A of about $11.05M in 2024-08 and total $17.9M; this appears only in aggregators and is unverified, so not recorded as a round. Recruiter postings claim profitability and $60M annualized revenue, unverified. Founder list differs by source (aggregators name other CEOs). Competitor search found only undated directory pages, so the list is empty. Latka claims no outside funding, contradicted by press.
